provenance.method: streaming rank-2 exclusion over all 7,439,040 four-qutrit stabilizer states

notes: Closes this cell as a route to the published exponent, which would need rank 2 here. The cell had no lower bound at all before. Excluding rank 2 over 7,439,040 stabilizer states is memory-bound rather than time-bound: holding them is 9.6 GB and the library enumerator doubles that by building a list before stacking, so the certificate holds nothing. Parallel vectors have identical canonical keys, since scaling q by lambda scales both (KEY.u) and (CAN.u) by lambda/|lambda|, so only a 16-byte key per state is kept. Equal keys are necessary for parallel, so no genuinely parallel pair can be missed; the reverse direction would only add a candidate. The raw enumeration repeats each state under several parametrisations, and repeats share a key, so states are deduplicated first by a 128-bit digest of the canonical form (dividing by the first nonzero entry puts every entry in {0, 1, w3, w3^2}); 12,249,468 raw reduce to exactly the expected 7,439,040. The exclusion rests on a margin: the closest any two of those keys come is 6.100e-07, against float error near 1e-15. The Strange state at m=2 is the positive control, where a rank-2 decomposition is known and the keys must collide.
